messages:
laura: quick Q — opened PR #4286 that touches service/handler and also adds our team to top-level CODEOWNERS. who needs to approve this? I tagged @miguel but not sure if CODEOWNERS changes require platform sign-off. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/PR/4286 :thinking_face:

miguel: generally, if you *modify* CODEOWNERS entries we ask a platform/owners-person to eyeball it. if it's just adding your service to an existing pattern sometimes it's fine. because the PR also changes infra-runtime files, the runtime owners should review that part. pinging @kevin for the runtime bits. :eyes:

kevin: hey — can take a look. quick question: is the CODEOWNERS change adding a new rule that could capture other paths or just the single service dir?

laura: just a single line: `services/our-service/    @our-team` — doesn't change existing globs. also included a tiny e2e fix. no infra config changes besides the handler code.

kevin: ok thanks. rule looks scoped. our policy: code changes are approved by the owning service/team; repo-level owner files (CODEOWNERS, top-level config) prefer a platform or repo-owner sign-off. two practical paths:
- split out the CODEOWNERS change into its own PR and tag repo/platform owners (fastest for audits)
- keep together but explicitly request both owners in the PR and wait for both approvals.

miguel: agree with split. operationally we've been allowing a single PR if all owners sign in the thread, but splitting avoids delays. if you keep it together, add a short note in PR body explaining scope and risk. also note: if an owner doesn't respond in 48h, escalate to `#engineering-owners` rotation (that's the fallback).

laura: splitting is fine — will open CODEOWNERS-only PR in a minute. for this PR can you approve the runtime changes so we can get the service fix in? CI passing locally.

kevin: approving the runtime code now. :white_check_mark: I left one tiny nits suggestion but it's non-blocking.

laura: awesome, thanks. I'll merge after CI and then open the CODEOWNERS PR and tag platform owners.

merge-bot: heads-up: if both approvals present and CI passes, autorebase/merge will queue. will wait for CODEOWNERS PR separately.

miguel: small doc note for others: when in doubt, split config/owner-file updates from functional changes. keeps approval routing simple and audit trail clean. :memo:

laura: noted. thanks everyone! :pray:
